verdict.rationale: Rootly documents the incident timeline as the authoritative chronological record, combining updates from people, systems, automations and communication channels. Retrospectives auto-draft a Curated Timeline from incident data, Slack and bridge transcripts, editable in a rich text editor. However, there is no explicit evidence of editing or annotating timeline events directly, and alert-specific capture is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit docs on editing/annotating timeline entries, explicit confirmation that alerts and chat decisions are auto-logged as timeline events, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, the incident timeline is captured automatically — alerts, actions, and chat decisions — and I can edit or annotate it afterwards

citations.quote: It brings together updates from people, systems, automations, and communication channels into one clear, chronological narrative.
Curated Timeline get drafted automatically from the incident's data, Slack channel, and bridge-call transcripts
Rootly includes a rich text editor in retrospectives that supports live incident data and real-time collaboration
